match.reason: No bank point teaches the trade-off of rewards like profit, independence and pride against the risks of losing money and time and of business closure; ecb-entrepreneur only touches risk as one part of defining an entrepreneur, and the investment and success cards cover different ideas.

draft.title: Risk and reward in starting a business
card: Starting a business can bring rewards. These include profit, which is money left after costs are paid, and independence, which means being your own boss.
Another reward is pride, the good feeling of building something that is your own and that people use.
Starting a business also has risks. The owner can lose the money they put in, and the time they spent on it.
Many new businesses close within a few years. Owners weigh the possible rewards against the risks before they start.
draft.remember: A new business can give profit, independence and pride, but the owner can also lose money and time.

a.q: Which of these is a risk of starting a business?
opts: The owner may lose the money they put in
The owner can choose how the business runs
The owner may earn a profit from sales
The owner may feel proud of what they built
a.why: Losing the money put into the business is a risk, because the business may not earn enough to pay it back. The other three are rewards: independence, profit and pride.
a.clue: Which one is something the owner could lose?

b.q: Priya leaves her job to open a bike repair shop in Ballarat. She spends her savings on tools. Which sentence best describes the risk she takes?
opts: The shop may close and her savings and time be lost
The shop may give her the freedom to set her own hours
The shop may make a profit once its costs are paid
The shop may give her pride in running her own business
b.why: The risk is that the shop does not work out, so the savings and time she put in are lost. The other options describe rewards that could come if the shop does well, even though they also look like good outcomes for Priya.
b.clue: A risk is something that could go wrong, not something good.

a.best: The owner may lose the money they put in

b.best: The shop may close and her savings and time be lost

problems.detail: The clue 'Which one is something the owner could lose?' uses 'lose', which appears in only one option, the right one. A student can pick it by matching words without knowing the idea of risk.
